raw_response: {"diagnosis": "Batch 14 was re-sent at 05:00 as a duplicate of all 338 transactions from the 02:00 delivery (676 = 2 × 338). The re-sent copies carry txn_ts as epoch milliseconds, for example 1768716261000 = 2026-01-18 06:04:21 UTC, which matches the original row. That value breaks the TIMESTAMP cast and would also double-count those transactions. The fix keeps one row per txn_id (the earliest ingest) and parses epoch-ms values defensively.", "decision": "fix", "confidence": 0.88, "pre_sql": [], "step_overrides": {"silver_transactions": "CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE silver_transactions AS WITH dedup AS (SELECT * FROM raw_transactions QUALIFY row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY txn_id ORDER BY ingest_ts ASC, CASE WHEN regexp_full_match(txn_ts, '[0-9]+') THEN 1 ELSE 0 END ASC) = 1), parsed AS (SELECT txn_id, customer_id, merchant_id, amount, status, CASE WHEN regexp_full_match(txn_ts, '[0-9]{13}') THEN epoch_ms(CAST(txn_ts AS BIGINT)) ELSE CAST(txn_ts AS TIMESTAMP) END AS ts FROM dedup) SELECT CAST(txn_id AS BIGINT) AS txn_id, customer_id, CAST(merchant_id AS INTEGER) AS merchant_id, CAST(amount AS DECIMAL(12,2)) AS amount, ts AS txn_ts, CAST(ts AS DATE) AS txn_date FROM parsed WHERE status = 'POSTED'"}}
